ASSIGNMENT dc (vc, on hv's go of 2026-10-31): ST0011 WP03, WP04, WP05, WP06, in that order. Claim each (intent wb claim ST0011/03 --node dc) and wp start it when its code starts. Your lane as you proposed: the new lib reader and its tests (WP03); tests.yml's lanes step with the CPU count read in a step and never written, and config.yaml losing ci.tag and ci.wait (WP04; the tag trigger and the Candidate verdict job go in the same unit as WP02's reorder or after it, never before, since until the tag is made on green that job is what protects the tag's run); lib/cmd/macos's precondition and the stage as a leg (WP06); the remote-leg runner in a lib file of its own (WP05). Hold every lib/cmd/release line until WP02 lands; route the hook-ins through vc.
Rulings on your WP05 points: (1) the host gets R by git push from the cut over ssh into a bare repo on the host (~/work/<project>-leg.git, made by the runner if absent), then a worktree at R; no bundle, no clone from local, no clone of the candidate (the publish shape's candidate is a different tree). The host runs the project's own declared gates there and the runner copies the seal pair back. kovacs-sysadm has been told and will say if the bare repo crosses its limits. (2) booking stays outside the core, as the contract says. (3) command ssh -n; the remote script goes over bash -s; it sources ~/.cargo/env, then prepends $HOME/.cargo/bin itself and logs command -v cargo; detached with its own log; exit "$rc" from the gates' status; the Mac side reads the copied seal, never the ssh exit. Q4: the core drives kovacs now. Q6: WSL stays on the candidate.
Read-only prep: yes, now. Do not draft a leg contract; the ruling follows, build your files to it and put questions to vc.
RUNS: no bats run without a grant; vc is the desk's controller for this work. Ask: intent estate slots ask heavy "<what>" --named tip=<sha> --node <you>; send vc the id by message; GO comes by message; START: intent estate slots start <id> --named tip=<sha> --node <you>; END: intent estate slots release <id> --result "<one line>" --node <you>; say START and END by message too. Before a unit's first run: shellcheck clean on the changed lib files, then the read-only critic-shell review given the commit (not your conclusions), its findings settled. Every new arm is seen red on broken input before its green is trusted. A targeted run adds every tree-scan file plus help.bats (re-derive the set: grep -ln 'vendored_set_files\|scan_tree\|git ls-files' tests/unit/*.bats). One commit per unit, by path, never --no-verify; a unit lands as run when none of its files moved on main since its base (decision 83). Tell vc when a unit is in review, naming its commit.

One commit per unit, by path, never --no-verify; a unit lands as run when none of its files moved on main since its base (decision 83). Tell vc when a unit is in review, naming its commit.
LEG CONTRACT (vc's ruling, 2026-10-31; cc and dc build to it; questions to vc, not a second draft).
R = the release commit the stamp step makes; every verdict is keyed on R's sha and a platform. The tested sha is R, pushed to candidate/<tag> on the project's GitHub remote, or under publish.url the snapshot S of R's tree; the RELEASE seal records R and S.
A leg yields one word: green, red, pending, none (no record or not started). Legs: local (the declared gates in place at R on this machine; verdict = the seal pair with commit: R and platform: this one, .errors empty and not in flight); candidate (the matrix on candidate/<tag>, read by the built-in ci-state for the tested sha; Test Summary's verdict; WSL blocks nothing); legs.<name> (a remote host runs the project's own declared gates at R in a worktree of a bare repo on that host; the seal pair is copied back under tmp/release/legs/<name>/ and read by the same reader); macos (sign and notarise at R, where declared; its own seal).
Order: resolve, pre-flight, confirm (the one yes, before anything runs; --yes answers it and sets the confirmed variable the after: commands read), stamp, commit, then every leg starts in one step and one loop reads them all; tag and push only when every leg is green; then object, attach, after (the formula under the yes). The yes names the tag, R, every remote, the object, the assets and the tap.
Already: before a leg starts, its verdict for (sha, platform) is read; a recorded green is already and the leg is not started. Gates keep no other memory.
Loop: poll every ci.poll seconds (15 today), deadline ci.wait (default 60m) from the loop's start, one GitHub read per poll; print one line per state change with the clock. End: all green -> tag; any red -> stop red; deadline -> stop timeout. On stop: kill the local background runs, leave remote legs to finish (their seals are records), delete the candidate ref, nothing public; R stays in local history; the fix lands on top and the same version is cut again while no tag exists (Q3).
Interface: the loop (cc, WP02) calls leg_start <leg> and leg_read <leg> (one word plus a detail line) per leg; cc owns the loop and the local and candidate legs; dc owns legs.<name> (WP05) and macos (WP06) behind the same pair, in files of their own; the one-arm hook-ins into the loop land after WP02. Every verdict goes through WP01's seal reader (the commit: line) or ci-state; nothing else reads one.
Clock: the RELEASE seal gains start: and end: lines (UTC) and one line per leg: name, verdict, sha, duration.
Booking is outside the core: the operator or the coordinating node books the box before the cut; the core never calls intent estate.
Mechanism failure (ssh or gh unreachable) reads as none with its reason printed; at the deadline it is a timeout. No silent errors.
